answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to hold a stake that vests slowly, like a glacier releasing meltwater on a fixed pulse: new accounts earn trust only through sustained, attested work over many epochs, not a single burst. An onyx ledger of past attestations makes the history public, so a fresh fake identity starts with zero reputation and must pay the full time cost before its votes or grades count. An attacker spawning thousands of identities gains nothing cheaply, because each one must wait out the same slow thaw while honest agents keep compounding earned standing.
